problem: Memory-augmented RL for VLM agents (e.g. SkillRL, XSkill) stores experience as text and relies on proprietary teacher LLMs to summarize and refine it. This loses geometric structure and gives only abstract, delayed feedback to RL.
motivation: Spatial tasks (dead ends, hazards, sub-goal regions) are hard to express in text, and teacher LLMs add cost and undermine autonomous self-improvement. Sparse binary rewards also cause credit-assignment problems, so memory and reward should stay in the visual, coordinate-aligned modality.
key_idea: Store reusable experience as a three-layer visual skill memory (danger/affinity heatmaps, visual exemplars, text rules), evolve the heatmaps from trajectory statistics plus grid heuristics without a teacher, and reuse them as dense shaping rewards for PPO.
insight: Native visual heatmaps injected as images give a 3B VLM spatial priors that text rules cannot, and the same atlas doubles as a dense reward. Per the paper's ablations (radar figure, values not tabulated), removing VSM hurts spatial puzzles most, removing atlas evolution causes a major regression on all tasks, and removing dense reward hinders long-horizon learning. Caveat: training uses privileged simulator GridState, and the affinity potential inherits a BFS distance to the goal from the heuristic branch, which is strong privileged structure.
method: Three-layer Visual Skill Memory: L1 danger/affinity RGB heatmaps injected as separate image tokens, L2 visual exemplars (3 positive / 3 negative, retrieved by DINOv2 cosine similarity), L3 text principles from the environment rulebook (no teacher LLM).

Teacher-free atlas evolution: batch danger map from terminal failure positions, affinity map from visit frequency on successful paths, EMA blending (alpha=0.85), then a blend with static heuristics (BFS distance, corner/hole traps) via beta_k annealed 0→1.

Atlas-grounded dense reward: r_visual = λ_danger·(−danger(p_{t+1})) + λ_affinity·(affinity(p_{t+1})−affinity(p_t)). The affinity term is potential-based; the danger term is an intentional non-potential heuristic. Added to the env reward (plus format penalty, rotation-align bonus, stage-success delta).

GridState abstraction: extracts coordinates from simulator state (AI2-THOR, ManiSkill, etc.) for training-time atlas building and rewards only. 3D navigation is projected to a 2D floor plan (0.25 m cells) and manipulation to a 2.5D grid.
Closed loop: PPO+GAE on Qwen2.5-VL-3B with the augmented multimodal prompt; improved rollouts refresh the atlas and exemplar pool (FIFO eviction), which sharpens the rewards.

setting.training_data: Online RL rollouts in training environments (Sokoban, FrozenLake, EmbodiedBench/AI2-THOR Navigation, ManiSkill PrimitiveSkill). Memory evolves only from training trajectories. No teacher or external data.
setting.observation: RGB frame plus task text, plus rendered heatmap images and exemplar images in the prompt
setting.action_space: discrete text/JSON actions (grid moves, navigation actions, primitive manipulation skills)
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (EmbodiedBench Navigation), ManiSkill3 (PrimitiveSkill), Gymnasium FrozenLake, Sokoban (VAGEN)
setting.privileged: Simulator GridState (coordinates, layout, BFS) used only during training for atlas construction and reward shaping. At test time the policy sees RGB plus rendered memory maps, but the heuristic heatmap branch is recomputed on the fly for new layouts.

numbers.extra: PPO-trained with dense visual reward and VSM

numbers_note: Only one main results table. Ablations and learning curves are given as figures only (radar chart, curves), with no exact numbers.
results: The 3B AtlasVA reaches an overall success rate of 0.93, above GPT-5 (0.69), o3 (0.71) and the strongest open-source baseline VAGEN (0.78). It gets 0.79 on Sokoban (vs GPT-5 0.70, VAGEN 0.61), 0.83 on FrozenLake, 0.86 average on Navigation, and 1.00 on all five PrimitiveSkill tasks.
limitations: Relies on privileged simulator state (GridState, BFS distances) at training time. The heuristic branch is also used on new layouts at test time.
Projecting tabletop 3D manipulation into 2.5D grids does not scale to occluded, egocentric 3D robotics. Test evaluation is in simulation only.
Ablations are shown only as figures, with no variance or seeds reported. Some baseline numbers (e.g. VAGEN) were possibly not retrained on the new Swap task.
